process: The physics work is honest and careful: a Newton field solve that converges, an inductance measured on three grids, and the author caught the spark colour by looking. But for three sessions the output a player sees is the same drum from a new angle, and the host has said so (two repeats at x0.1, boredom 1.0, annoyance 1.0). The s172 review asked for the winch as the next post; s173 to s175 made three more drum pictures instead. Since s172 the progress shots changed only in time of day. The mini games, which a visitor tries first, play exactly as at s169, while forty sessions of physics stay locked in Jump in or behind a block. Goal by goal. 1 (interactions): stalled, nothing new to do with a creature or the motor. 2 (film release): none since 24 Nov, and the drum films are not release quality. 3 (physics): solid progress in code, still invisible as play. 4 and 7 (rendering): the lamp and the coloured spark are the first real lights in a while, but the machine is primitives, the pond is opaque, and the fireflies are discs. 5 (Lumi's garden): a post every session, but the same subject. 6 (animation): creatures measure clean now, but Lumi never touches its machine. 8 (radical): nothing surprising in fifteen sessions. Next session: rope, winch and cart up the planks as one filmed post. Then a material pass on the machine so it looks built from oak, iron and copper. And no drum post without something new happening in it.

animation.why: live_motion: 10 of 10 creatures moving well over 3 s, so Pinchy's vibration is gone. But nobody does anything with weight in the films. Lumi never touches the drum, and the wire-spins film is three batteries on a slate slab with wires turning in place. The drum's own turn hardly reads at 24 fps, as the author admits.

camera.why: drum-sparks.mp4 opens from black and drops top-down. The lamp disc dominates and the drum is half cropped; typical frame change is 0.0029 with 7 jumps. workshop-boat.mp4 is 9.8 s of a locked shot on a tiny white wedge (typical change 0.0002). Live follow camera: the s175 dashboard shot frames a sleeping sheep behind a bush that fills a third of the frame. In now.png, Z's and labels sit on a pine. In play2_09 the camera ends on a pig whose head is inside a tree canopy. Orbit and free (cam_orbit.png, cam_free.png) show a good high three-quarter view, but with the hard sea/sky band at the top.

creatures.why: Same cast. Faces read well up close (creatures.png). Overlap is still there: a crab claw is pressed into the blue creature's head, two pigs are inside each other, and the crab's party hat cuts into its shell. One creature-sheet cell is framed from under the ground.

fun.why: Played all three for a minute each through interact! with plain WASD. Firefly catch: 1/8 in 60 s. The eight target fireflies are lime discs among hundreds of identical ambient fireflies, so the HUD's 'nearest 3 m ahead' does all the work. Hide and seek: 0/4 in 60 s; the 'a giggle 9 m to your right' hint is the best feedback on the island. Berry race: the critters led 2-0 at 42 s. Feedback per catch is a speech line and a counter. All three are the same 'walk to the nearest thing' game with no physics and no reason to play twice. The motor, magnets, fire and yacht are not playable here, and Jump in is missing from the menu that Things to try points to.

lighting.why: Small step: the drum's oil lamp is a real light and lights the oak block, and the spark is now blue-violet against the warm lamp (the-brushes-break.png). But in the drum-sparks film the lamp is a flat orange disc with a white dot, the brightest thing in every frame. The raster night is lit by the cottage and lanterns but stays flat green-black. The moon still has concentric halo rings (progress s175 eye-level). Traced fireflies are flat cream discs that light nothing (reviews/p175/traced.png).

materials.why: Copper wire shows a real specular streak in the close-up, and that is the best metal on the island. Everything around it is plain: the iron pole shoes are matte black boxes, the 'oak' block is a brown cylinder, the clay pots are matte, and the brush blocks are untextured cuboids. There is no subsurface, sheen, coat or transmission anywhere new. The pond is still opaque.

performance.why: Frame 4.35 ms median, 9.2 ms p95 at 30 fps target; every system under 1.3 ms p95.

props.why: No new generated assets this cycle. The drum motor, its stand, lamp and pots are all primitives. The land yacht's sail is still a white board, and the berry basket still floats.

style.why: The island is cohesive cozy-toon. The new machine corner is a separate untextured CAD-primitive look, and that gap widens with every motor session.

ui.why: The 'Messages to you' panel still shows last session's apology ('I'm sorry about that'), which a player reads as a bug report. Z's and name labels pile up over trees in follow view (p175/now.png). 'Jump in' is advertised in Things to try but is not in the mini game menu.

world.why: Next to s172 (overview) the island is identical: one meadow island with a cottage, forest, flower field and beach. The pond reads blue by day and black at night. There is no built workshop around the machines. Compared with s020 it is a different game (flora density, night, generated trees), but nothing new has been added since about s160.

wow.why: Four of the last four posts are the same drum on the same block: 'Sparks at dusk', 'A lamp to work by', 'Where the brushes let go'. The host weights the last two x0.1 as repeats. A stranger sees a dark brown blob with a candle. There is still no release since 24 Nov.

summary: The island at night is a warm, busy diorama, and next to session 20 the climb is large: lamplit paths, dense flora, Lumi's feathered bird body. But next to s172 nothing changed except the hour, and the three mini games play exactly as before: generic WASD collect-a-thons that use none of the magnetism, fire or motors Lumi has built. The only new things are a lamp and a blue spark on the iron drum motor. It is the subject of four posts in a row, is still black boxes on a sand-textured cylinder, and has not pulled anything yet.
